q: The entropy method in ergodic theory (Sinai, Ornstein) uses the notion of 'finitely determined' (or VWB) processes. A process {Xₙ} is finitely determined if:
opts: It is determined by finitely many variables
For any ε > 0 there exists δ > 0 and N such that processes matching the joint distribution of X₁,…,X_N within δ are within ε of the original in the d̄-metric
exp: Finitely determined (Ornstein): the process can be 'approximated' by finite windows with respect to the d̄-metric (the Ornstein metric). Bernoulli processes are finitely determined. VWB implies FD, and FD implies the process is Bernoulli—this was Ornstein's key technical lemma in proving his isomorphism theorem.
